title: Tomato Sauce, Canned, with Salt Added

content.title: About
content.content: Tomato sauce, canned with added salt, is made from ripe tomatoes that are pureed, cooked with salt and sometimes a touch of sugar and spices, then sealed in airtight glass or metal jars. The sauce has a thick, smooth texture, bright red color, and a characteristic tomato aroma.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes used for the sauce are often grown in greenhouses, allowing a year‑round supply.
Canning preserves most of the vitamin C and lycopene – a powerful antioxidant found in tomatoes.
Salt not only enhances flavor but also acts as a preservative, extending shelf life.
Tomato sauce is a base for many dishes: pasta, pizza, stews, soups, and marinades.
In some regions, herbs like basil, oregano, or garlic are added, but the basic version contains none.

items.title: Rich in lycopene
items.content: Lycopene is a carotenoid with antioxidant properties that may support heart and prostate health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C helps strengthen the immune system and improves iron absorption.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Tomato sauce contains virtually no fat, making it suitable for low‑calorie diets.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium aids in fluid balance and helps maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Tomatoes provide dietary fiber, which promotes healthy bowel function.

items.title: High salt content
items.content: Excessive salt intake can raise blood pressure and strain the kidneys.

items.title: Tomato allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to tomatoes.

items.title: Bisphenol A in packaging
items.content: Metal cans may contain trace amounts of BPA, so choose products from reputable manufacturers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Use tomato sauce as a base for pasta, pizza, meat dishes, soups, and stews. Heat it in a pan, add spices to taste, or blend with other sauces to create new flavor combinations.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store unopened jars in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. After opening, keep refrigerated and consume within 5‑7 days. Discard if you notice mold, off‑odor, or other signs of spoilage.
